title: Fažana With a Dog 2027: Beaches, Rules & Costs
metaDescription: Fažana with a dog: official dog beaches, Brijuni rules, old town and restaurant etiquette, accommodation fees, best months, vets and EU pet passport rules.
content:
## Which beaches in Fažana are official dog beaches?

Fažana has several marked dog beaches (plaža za pse). All are pebble or rock, and none has lifeguards or sun loungers.

### Bi Dog Beach
Bi Dog Beach sits on the left side of the BiVillage holiday centre at Dragonja 115. It is free to enter, with no time limits for dogs. The strip is about 50 m long and has a dog shower. It has no natural shade, so bring a parasol. It is open to non-guests because it lies next to the public walking path.

### Dog beach on Aleja maslina
This beach is on the Fažana promenade and is signposted as pet-friendly. It has pebbles, smooth rock, pine shade for much of the day and a gentle entry into the sea. There are waste-bag dispensers but no dog shower. People can use the showers and toilets at nearby Batana Beach. The pebbles are coarse, so a mat or water shoes help.

### Perer and Hidrobaza
Perer is about 1.4 km from Bi Dog Beach. It has natural shade and a mix of pebbles and concrete slabs. Hidrobaza is a further dog beach at the northern end of the promenade. Pineta is another dog beach on the municipal tourist list.

## Are dogs allowed on other beaches in Fažana?

Dogs are generally not allowed on regular public swimming beaches in Croatia during the season, and Fažana follows this. Look for the pet symbol on signs. Beaches with a Blue Flag ban dogs across Istria. Stay on the marked dog stretches and keep a leash and waste bags with you.

## Dogs in the old town and on the promenade

Dogs are welcome in Fažana's old town, around the harbour and on the breakwater. The town lists these among its dog-friendly points of interest, along with Sardela park. Two walks suit dogs well:

- **Promenade with views of Brijuni:** an easy 5 km one-way walk from Hidrobaza to Martuline beach, mostly under pines.
- **Staza dobrih vibracija:** a 5 km circular walking and cycling path.

The old town is small. Keep dogs leashed on the quay in summer, when day-trippers queue for the Brijuni boats.

## Dogs in restaurants

Terraces along the harbour usually accept dogs, and indoor dining rooms often do not. Ask before sitting down. Tables near the water get full afternoon sun in July and August, so choose a shaded one and ask for a bowl of water. Fresh fish, the local speciality, is easy to share with a dog only if you skip the bones.

## Brijuni National Park with a dog

Dogs are allowed in Brijuni, with strict limits:

- A dog ticket costs €15.
- Dogs must be leashed at all times. The park's rules require dogs to be older than 6 months, weigh up to 30 kg and have a pet passport with proof of vaccinations.
- Dogs may not enter the Safari Park, the tourist train or museums.
- Dogs may be walked only in permitted zones, mainly around the Veliki Brijun harbour. They may swim in the water 50 m from the southern breakwater towards Jupiter Beach.
- Dogs are allowed on outdoor restaurant terraces but not in indoor dining areas.

The park's own boat from the Fažana quay is the only public access. The crossing takes about 15 minutes and cars are not carried.

The official programme is built around the train and the Safari Park, which dogs cannot use. The €15 ticket is therefore poor value for most dog owners. A private or semi-private boat tour from Fažana that accepts dogs is the better way to see the archipelago.

## Ferries, boats and catamarans

Fažana has no car ferry. Several private operators from the port run Brijuni panoramic tours and dolphin cruises, and they advertise dogs as welcome. Private panoramic tours are priced per group, for example €250 for up to 6 people on a 40-minute tour. Confirm the dog policy when booking, because rules differ by operator and vessel.

## What does accommodation charge for a dog?

Expect a dog fee of roughly €5–15 per night in private apartments, hotels and campsites. Some hosts charge a one-off cleaning fee instead. Some properties cap the number or size of dogs. Larger holiday centres, such as BiVillage, advertise themselves as dog-friendly. Book places with a fenced garden or ground floor if the dog is large. Always confirm the dog fee in writing, as it is often missing from listings.

## Summer heat and the best months

July and August bring hot days, often above 30°C, and sea temperatures near 27°C. Asphalt and quay stones get too hot for paws by midday. Walk before 9:00 or after 19:00 and rest in the shade in between.

The best months are April to June and September to October. Water is swimmable from late May, crowds are smaller and dog beaches are quiet. Never leave a dog in a parked car.

## Vet basics

Pula is about 8 km from Fažana and has the nearest clinics. Save a clinic's number and check its opening hours before arriving, since weekend cover varies. Croatia's general emergency number is 112. Carry the vaccination record and ask about ticks and sandfly (leishmaniasis) prevention before travelling, because both are present in Istria in warm months.

## EU pet passport rules for driving in

- The dog needs an ISO microchip, implanted before or on the date of rabies vaccination.
- Rabies vaccination must be valid. The dog must be at least 12 weeks old at vaccination, and a 21-day wait applies after the first shot.
- Dogs need an EU pet passport. Travellers from outside the EU need an animal health certificate, as the passport is only valid for EU-issued documents.
- A maximum of five pets can travel together for non-commercial purposes.
- Tapeworm treatment is not required for Croatia.

Check the rules for any transit countries, as some require extra treatments. Rules can change, so verify with the vet or the national authority before departure.

## Verdict: how dog-friendly is Fažana?

Fažana is among the most dog-friendly towns in Istria, scoring about 4.5 out of 5. It has several free dog beaches, a shaded promenade and terraces that accept dogs. The main weakness is Brijuni, where dogs are heavily restricted. It is a very good choice for dog owners from April to June and September to October. In July and August it suits dogs that tolerate heat and need shade.

faq.question: Does Fažana have an official dog beach?
faq.answer: Yes. Fažana has several, including Bi Dog Beach at BiVillage, a dog beach on Aleja maslina by the promenade, Perer and Hidrobaza. Entry is free and none has lifeguards.

faq.question: Can I take my dog to Brijuni National Park from Fažana?
faq.answer: Yes, on a leash and with a €15 dog ticket. Dogs may not enter the Safari Park, tourist train or museums. They are limited to permitted zones, mainly around the Veliki Brijun harbour.

faq.question: Are dogs allowed in restaurants in Fažana?
faq.answer: Usually on outdoor terraces, not indoors. Ask the staff first and choose a shaded table, as harbour terraces get strong sun in summer.

faq.question: How much does accommodation charge for a dog in Fažana?
faq.answer: Typically €5–15 per night, sometimes a one-off cleaning fee instead. Confirm the amount and any size limits before booking.

faq.question: What is the best time to visit Fažana with a dog?
faq.answer: April to June and September to October. Temperatures are milder, the sea is swimmable from late May and the beaches are quieter than in July and August.

faq.question: What documents does my dog need to enter Croatia?
faq.answer: An ISO microchip, a valid rabies vaccination and an EU pet passport, or a health certificate for non-EU travellers. No tapeworm treatment is required for Croatia.

quickAnswer: Fažana is very dog-friendly. It has several marked dog beaches, including Bi Dog Beach, a promenade with views of Brijuni, and boat tours that accept dogs. Restaurants usually allow dogs on terraces. Brijuni National Park charges €15 per dog and restricts where dogs can go. Come in April–June or September–October.
